title: Arrays & Strings
description: Lists of values, character text, indexes, and simple loops.

screens.heading: A list in a box
screens.body:
An array is a list that lives in one variable. You put values in order, then grab them later by position.

Think of a row of cubbies. Each cubby holds one thing. The whole row is the array.
screens.keyPoint: An array is one variable that holds several values in order.

screens.heading: Indexes start at 0
screens.body:
The first item is not number 1. It is number 0. That number is the index.

So colours[0] is "teal". colours[1] is "purple". The last index is always length minus 1.
screens.keyPoint: The first slot is index 0. The last slot is length - 1.

screens.heading: Change one slot
screens.body:
You can replace a value without rebuilding the whole list. Point at the index, then assign a new value.

If you ask for an index that does not exist, JavaScript gives you undefined — it does not crash.
screens.keyPoint: array[index] = value replaces whatever was in that slot.

screens.heading: Strings are also sequences
screens.body:
A string is text. Under the hood it is a sequence of characters, and those characters also have indexes starting at 0.

You can read one character with brackets. You cannot assign into a string the way you assign into an array — strings are immutable.
screens.keyPoint: Strings have indexes too, but you cannot rewrite a character in place.

screens.heading: Slice copies a piece
screens.body:
slice(start, end) copies a section of an array into a new array. The start index is included. The end index is not.

The original array stays the same. That makes slice a safe way to peek at a range.
screens.keyPoint: slice copies. The end index is not included.

screens.heading: Walk the list with a loop
screens.body:
When you want every item, do not type colours[0], colours[1], colours[2] by hand. Use a loop.

A for loop with i going from 0 to length - 1 visits each index once. That pattern shows up everywhere.
screens.keyPoint: Loop from 0 while i is less than length so you never skip or overshoot.

checkIn.prompt: In const pets = ["cat", "dog", "owl"], what is pets[1]?
checkIn.explanation: Index 1 is the second item because counting starts at 0.
